API 570 4th Edition 2024 — Eligibility, Exam Structure, and What Closed-Book vs Open-Book Actually Tests

API 570 4th Edition 2024 eligibility per §1.3 requires (a) BS degree in engineering + 1 year applicable experience, (b) 2-year degree + 2 years, (c) high school + 3 years, or (d) other + 5 years — with demonstrable involvement in design, fabrication, repair, alteration, or inspection of in-service piping. The exam runs Pearson VUE computer-based, 7.5 hours total: 3.25-hour closed-book on inspection practices, repair, alteration, rerating, and pressure-test; 4.25-hour open-book on API 570, API RP 571, API RP 574, API RP 577, API RP 578, API 579-1/ASME FFS-1, ASME B31.3, and ASME Section V/IX. Pass mark 70%. Atlantis Academy first-pass rate 96% across 2024-2026 — supported by a closed-book damage-mechanism flash drill (sulfidation, naphthenic-acid, HTHA, amine cracking, sour-water cracking, chloride SCC, MIC, CUI, HIC/SOHIC) and an open-book navigation drill (we time-test you on locating API 570 §6.3 CUI tables, API 571 §4.4.2 sulfidation rate curves, API 579-1 Part 5 LTA assessment, and ASME B31.3 §304 thickness equations in under 90 seconds each).

§5 Inspection and Testing Practices — TML Grids, UT Thickness, and the Bracketed-Reading Trap

API 570 §5.5 inspection practices anchor the inspector's daily work — thickness-measurement-location (TML) grids per §5.5.2 with locations at elbows, tees, reducers, and downstream of injection points; ultrasonic thickness measurement per ASME B&PV Section V Article 23 SE-797 with calibration on a stepped wedge traceable to NIST; bracketed CUI inspections per §5.5.7 with insulation removal at the 6 o'clock + 12 o'clock positions across 6-12 inch strips minimum per API 583 §6.4. The bracketed-reading trap: inspectors who log a single nominal thickness without the 4-point average around the TML get caught at the next FFS review per API 579-1 Part 5 §5.4.2.2 when localised metal loss is reassessed and the reading turns out to be a high-side outlier. Atlantis Academy drills TML protocol with Olympus 38DL-Plus + Sonatest D70 + GE DMS Go+ on real refinery mock-ups — see Atlantis training and Atlantis Academy.

§6 Frequency and Extent — CUI, Injection-Point, Soil-Air-Interface, and Dead-Leg Schedules

API 570 §6.3 sets inspection-frequency tables based on piping classification (Class 1 highly toxic / flammable, Class 2 services, Class 3 low-hazard). Class 1 internal/on-stream interval = half remaining life or 5 years, whichever is less. CUI inspection per §6.3.5 mandates extra scrutiny on lines operating between -12°C and 175°C carbon steel, -12°C and 150°C stainless — the temperature window where moisture condenses against ferritic steel and CUI rate per API 571 §4.3.5 spikes. Injection-point circuits per §5.5.3 require thickness scans on 12 pipe diameters downstream + 25% of upstream — Marathon Petroleum MP-ITP-0037 §4.2 and Aramco SAES-L-132 §6 mandate quarterly thickness at injection points carrying water washes, caustic, or amines. Soil-air interface per §6.3.4 — 12-inch above and 12-inch below grade — catches the localised pitting that wipes 30% of buried-pipe wall in a single 18-month cycle if neglected. Dead legs per §5.5.5 — flag every dead leg ≥0.5 m, scan at high and low points, treat as candidates for MIC per API 571 §5.1.1.6. Atlantis builds the inspection-schedule generator inside Atlantis ERP with §6.3 logic embedded so the inspector cannot under-schedule a CUI line.

§7 Inspection Data Evaluation and §8 Repairs — Corrosion Rates, Remaining Life, and the FFS Handoff

§7.1.2 short-term corrosion rate = (t_previous - t_actual) / time between, long-term = (t_initial - t_actual) / years in service; the inspector uses the higher of the two to drive next-inspection date. Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required) / corrosion rate. When t_actual approaches t_required and remaining life falls below 4 years, §7.6 mandates an FFS Level 1/2/3 per API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 Part 4 (general metal loss) or Part 5 (localised metal loss) with MAWP recalculation. §8 repair, alteration, and rerating must be performed under §8.1 by ASME B31.3-qualified welders with WPS/PQR per ASME Section IX QW-200, and §8.2.7 requires PWHT per ASME B31.3 §331 for chrome-moly and certain stainless services. The handoff from API 570 inspection to API 579 FFS is where most piping programs leak value — Atlantis runs the joint workflow via Atlantis API 579 FFS consulting and RBI per API 580/581.

§9 Pressure Tests, Documentation, and the Audit Trail That Saves Your Certificate

§9 pressure tests — hydrostatic per ASME B31.3 §345 at 1.5×design pressure for ferritic + 1.3× for non-ferritic, hold time 10 minutes minimum, visual inspection of every joint at hold pressure with no leakage or weeping permitted. Pneumatic tests per §9.4 only when hydro is impractical, special safety controls per ASME B31.3 §345.5. Documentation under §7.4 — every inspection record must trace inspector signature, date, instrument serial number + calibration date, TML reading, corrosion rate, remaining life, and next-inspection-date computation. Atlantis ERP's piping-inspection module wires §7.4 documentation into a single audit trail with WPS/PQR records, RBI per API 580/581 integration, and FFS package generation for handoff to API 579 FFS.

Sour-Service Hardness Limits per NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 — The Trap on Page-One Welds

NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sour-service hardness limits — 22 HRC max on carbon steel weld + HAZ, 28 HRC for some L80 grades — drive the rejection criterion on any weld facing wet H2S service. The trap on API 570 exams + on-job: assuming PWHT alone delivers acceptable hardness. Reality — base-metal carbon equivalent CE per IIW formula + heat-input control during welding + cooling rate + PWHT cycle all interact, and a single hard spot in HAZ exceeding 22 HRC = sulfide-stress-cracking initiation site per API RP 571 §5.1.2.4. Aramco SAEP-1112 §6.5 + ADNOC GMTS-100 §7.3 + Shell DEP 31.38.30.31 sour-service piping all enforce hardness mapping with portable Equotip or UCI hardness on every weld + HAZ per ASTM E110 / ASTM A1038. KOC Shah Gas Plant 15% H2S service drives hardness mapping on 100% of welds. Atlantis Academy drills the hardness-mapping protocol with portable hardness instruments alongside the SNT-TC-1A 2024 / CP-189-2020 syllabus.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: What is the realistic pass rate for first-time API 570 candidates?

A: ASNT/API official first-pass averages around 50-55% globally. Atlantis Academy first-pass rate is 96% across 2024-2026 cohorts due to closed-book damage-mechanism drilling and timed open-book navigation. Free retake-grade backstop included.

Q2: Do I need API 510 first or can I jump straight to API 570?

A: No prerequisite — API 570 is independently eligible per §1.3. Most piping inspectors hold API 570 + API 510 + API 653 stacked; the order depends on your asset portfolio.

Q3: How does CUI inspection per §6.3.5 actually work on insulated lines without removing all insulation?

A: Strip inspection on 6 o'clock + 12 o'clock at 6-12 inch strips, profile RT or pulsed-eddy-current screening per API 583 §6.4, plus systematic removal at termination points, hangers, and any wet-jacket signs. Atlantis ERP CUI module schedules the strip locations automatically against API 571 §4.3.5 temperature windows.

Q4: When should I escalate from API 570 thickness data to API 579 FFS?

A: When remaining life under §7.1 drops below 4 years, when localised metal loss exceeds 0.3 of nominal thickness over a critical-thickness profile per API 579-1 Part 5 §5.4.2.2, or when a TML reading triggers §7.6 evaluation. Atlantis runs the FFS escalation as a single ERP workflow.

Q5: How often must I recertify and what does it cost?

A: Recertification every 3 years per API 570 §1.4 with body-of-knowledge re-exam. Pricing varies by region and scope — request a tailored quote within 24 hours.

Q6: Do Aramco / ADNOC / Shell accept API 570 alone for piping turnarounds?

A: Aramco SAES-L-310 §5 and ADNOC GMTS-100 §7 require API 570 inspector for in-service piping; Shell DEP 31.38.01.31 mirrors. ASNT Level II UT/MT/PT is required for the technician layer underneath.

Q7: Is there an online cohort?

A: Yes — Atlantis Academy runs hybrid online + practical-week cohorts quarterly. See Atlantis LMS.
